finding.claim: dropTable never enforces its 'dba' role check: Authorize's error return is discarded, so any request that reaches /admin/drop with a context user runs the DROP regardless of roles.
finding.source: Any HTTP client that reaches the /admin/drop route (api.go:44). The user object is read from request context key "user" (api.go:22), which is set by middleware that is not in this repository.

trace.note: main registers /admin/drop -> dropTable with no authorization wrapper.
u := userFrom(r) loads the user from context; no nil or role check here.
Authorize(u, "dba") is called but its error return is ignored, so execution continues whether or not the user has the role.
runSQL executes the DROP with attacker-chosen table name.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is itself correct: exact-match role comparison, returns error when role absent. The bug is only that its result is discarded. Compared line by line with vacuum (api.go:33-36), which checks the error and returns 403. No other middleware or wrapper for /admin/drop exists in this repo; the auth context setter is outside the repo and unverified. The route has no CSRF protection: FormValue (api.go:27) reads query-string params for GET requests too, so a state-changing GET is possible if the upstream auth is cookie-based.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role control and it is effectively bypassed: its error return is discarded as a bare statement at api.go:26, unlike vacuum's checked call at api.go:33-35. No authorization wrapper is applied to /admin/drop at api.go:44. The upstream context-user middleware is outside the repo and unverified, but it only establishes identity, not the dba role, so it does not block a non-dba user.
verdict.reason: The role check at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error is discarded, so runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 executes for any user reaching /admin/drop registered at api.go:44, including authenticated users without the dba role; the only remaining gate is out-of-repo middleware that does not check roles.

finding.claim: SQL injection in dropTable: the request parameter 't' is concatenated directly into a DDL statement with no validation, allowlist, or identifier quoting.
finding.source: HTTP request parameter "t" read via r.FormValue at api.go:27 (query string or form body), fully attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: runSQL at api.go:27, which executes the concatenated SQL.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into "DROP TABLE " + value and passed to runSQL.
runSQL(string) is the sink. In this repo it is an empty stub, so nothing runs here; the injection is real only if the production runSQL executes the string as SQL.

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, quoting or parameterization on the path. Reachability requires passing F1 today (any authenticated user). Once F1 is fixed, exploitation still requires the dba role, so this remains an injection in a privileged path. Whether multi-statement input is accepted depends on the database driver, which is not in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error return is discarded, so it is not a guard. Nothing else on the path validates, allowlists, quotes, or parameterizes r.FormValue("t") before the concatenation at api.go:27. runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub with no protection.
verdict.reason: The concatenation of r.FormValue("t") into "DROP TABLE " at api.go:27 has no effective control, since the Authorize check at api.go:26 is a discarded bare call that never blocks the request; the sink at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the injection is exploitable only once the production runSQL executes the string as SQL.
